chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Dawud, from a man, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about an amulet/supplication for protection that is hung upon a menstruating woman. He said: “There is no harm in it.” And he said: “She may recite it and write it, but she must not touch it.”

key_terms.التَّعْوِيذِ: a protective supplication or written amulet used for seeking refuge
key_terms.الْحَائِضِ: a woman in the state of menstruation
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection in doing so

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman wear, recite, or write a ta'widh, and is she allowed to touch it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a menstruating woman and a written ta'widh. It states that there is no problem in hanging it on her, and that she may recite and write it, but she should not touch it directly.
